title.zh: 卷七十八 列傳第八: 耶律夷臘葛 蕭海璃 蕭護思 蕭思溫 蕭繼先
title.en: Volume 78 Biographies 8: Yelu Yilage, Xiao Haili, Xiao Husi, Xiao Siwen, Xiao Jixian
title.raw: 卷七十八 列傳第八: 耶律夷臘葛 蕭海璃 蕭護思 蕭思溫 蕭繼先 Volume 78 Biographies 8: Yelu Yilage, Xiao Haili, Xiao Husi, Xiao Siwen, Xiao Jixian

sentences.zh: 耶律夷臘葛蕭海璃蕭護思蕭思溫蕭繼先

translations.literal: Yelü Yilage, Xiao Haili, Xiao Husi, Xiao Siwen, and Xiao Jixian
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Yilage; Xiao Haili; Xiao Husi; Xiao Siwen; Xiao Jixian

sentences.zh: 蕭海璃，字寅的哂，其先遙輦氏時為本部夷離堇。

translations.literal: Xiao Haili, style name Yin de Shen — his forebears in Yaonian clan times served as yilizhen of their tribal division.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Haili, whose style name was Yin de Shen, came from a line that in Yaonian clan times had held the tribal chieftaincy of their division.

sentences.zh: 父塔列，天顯間為本部令穩。

translations.literal: His father Tale during the Tianxian era served as lingwen of the tribal division.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tale served as lingwen of the division during the Tianxian era.

sentences.zh: 海璃貌魁偉，膂力過人。

translations.literal: Haili in appearance was towering and imposing; his physical strength surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: Haili was imposing in stature, with strength that surpassed ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 天祿間，娶明王安端女藹因翁主。

translations.literal: During the Tianlu era he married Princess Aiyin, daughter of Prince of Ming An Duan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianlu era he married Princess Aiyin, daughter of the Prince of Ming, An Duan.

sentences.zh: 應歷初，察割亂，藹因連坐，繼娶嘲瑰翁主。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yingli, Chage's rebellion — Aiyin was implicated by association; he then married Princess Chaogui.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yingli era, when Chage rebelled, Aiyin was implicated with him; Haili then married Princess Chaogui.

sentences.zh: 上以近戚，嘉其勤篤，命預北府宰相選。

translations.literal: The emperor, as a near kinsman, commended his diligence and constancy and ordered him to participate in Northern Chancellery chancellor selection.
translations.idiomatic: As a close kinsman, the emperor praised his diligence and ordered him into the pool for Northern Chancellery chancellor selection.

sentences.zh: 頃之，總知軍國事。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he had overall charge of military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was placed in overall charge of military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 時諸王多坐反逆，海璃為人廉謹，達政體，每被命按獄，多得其情，人無冤者，由是知名。

translations.literal: At the time many princes were convicted of treason; Haili as a man was scrupulous and cautious, understood the substance of government — whenever ordered to investigate cases he mostly got the true facts, and no one suffered wrongful punishment; thereby he became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: When many princes were being convicted of treason, Haili's scrupulous character and grasp of government meant that whenever he was assigned to investigate a case he usually uncovered the truth, and no one was wrongfully punished — for which he became well known.

sentences.zh: 漢主劉承鈞每遣使入貢，必別致幣物，詔許受之。

translations.literal: Each time the Han ruler Liu Chengjun sent envoys to offer tribute he would separately send gifts; an edict permitted accepting them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Northern Han ruler Liu Chengjun sent tribute envoys, he would also send separate gifts, and an edict permitted Haili to accept them.

sentences.zh: 年五十卒，帝湣悼，輟朝二日。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty; the emperor mourned him and suspended court for two days.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty. The emperor mourned him and suspended court for two days.

sentences.zh: 蕭護思，字延寧，世為北院吏，累遷御史中丞，總典群牧部籍。

translations.literal: Xiao Husi, style name Yanning — his family for generations were Northern Court clerks; he rose in succession to Vice Censor-in-Chief and had overall charge of the herd registers of the Group Herds Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Husi, style name Yanning, came from a family that had served for generations as Northern Court clerks. He rose to Vice Censor-in-Chief and oversaw the herd registers of the Group Herds Directorate.

sentences.zh: 應歷初，遷左客省使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yingli he was transferred to Left Commissioner of the Guest Service.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yingli era he was made Left Commissioner of the Guest Service.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時諸王多坐事系獄，上以護思有才幹，詔窮治，稱旨，改北院樞密使，仍命世預宰相選。

translations.literal: At the time many princes were imprisoned for offenses; the emperor, because Husi had ability, ordered thorough investigation — it pleased him; he was changed to Northern Privy Commissioner and still ordered his line to participate in chancellor selection.
translations.idiomatic: When many princes were imprisoned for crimes, the emperor, finding Husi capable, ordered a thorough investigation that pleased him. Husi was made Northern Privy Commissioner, and his line was still enrolled in chancellor selection.

sentences.zh: 護思辭曰：「臣子孫賢否未知，得一客省使足矣。」

translations.literal: Husi declined, saying: "Whether my descendants are worthy is unknown — to obtain one Guest Service commissioner suffices."
translations.idiomatic: Husi declined: "I cannot know whether my descendants will prove worthy — one Guest Service commissioner is enough for them."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 上晚歲酗酒，用刑多濫，護思居要地，齪齪自保，未嘗一言匡救，議者以是少之。

translations.literal: In the emperor's later years he drank heavily and punishments were excessive; Husi occupied a key post, timidly guarding himself alone, never once speaking to correct and save — critics for this held him in low regard.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the emperor drank heavily and punishments grew excessive. Husi held a key post but only huddled in self-protection and never once spoke up to correct him — for which critics despised him.

sentences.zh: 年五十七卒。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 蕭思溫，小字寅古，宰相敵魯之族弟忽沒裏之子。

translations.literal: Xiao Siwen, childhood name Yingu — son of Humoli, younger cousin on the clan side of Chancellor Diru.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Siwen, whose childhood name was Yingu, was the son of Humoli, a younger cousin of Chancellor Diru's clan.

sentences.zh: 通書史。

translations.literal: He was versed in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He was well versed in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 太宗時為奚禿裏太尉，尚燕國公主，為群牧都林牙。

translations.literal: Under Taizong he served as Xi Tuli Grand Commandant, married the Princess of Yan, and became Chief Intendant of the Herds Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizong he served as Grand Commandant of the Xi Tuli, married the Princess of Yan, and became Chief Intendant of the Herds Directorate.

sentences.zh: 思溫在軍中，握齱修邊幅，僚佐皆言非將帥才。

translations.literal: Siwen in the army was fastidious about propriety and appearance; his staff all said he lacked the talent of a commander.
translations.idiomatic: In camp Siwen was fussy about dress and decorum, and his staff all said he was no commander.

sentences.zh: 尋為南京留守。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Southern Capital intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed intendant of the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 初，周人攻揚州，上遣思溫躡其後，憚暑不敢進，拔緣邊數城而還。

translations.literal: Initially when the Zhou attacked Yangzhou, the emperor sent Siwen to trail them; fearing the summer heat he did not advance, took several border towns, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou first attacked Yangzhou, the emperor sent Siwen to follow in their rear, but he shrank from the summer heat and would not advance, seized a few border towns, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後周師來侵，圍馮母鎮，勢甚張。

translations.literal: Later Zhou armies came to invade and besieged Fengmu garrison; their momentum was very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou forces invaded again, besieged Fengmu garrison, and their momentum was formidable.

sentences.zh: 思溫請益兵，帝報曰：「敵來，則與統軍司並兵拒之；

translations.literal: Siwen requested additional troops; the emperor replied: "When the enemy comes, join the Commissariat forces and resist together;
translations.idiomatic: Siwen asked for reinforcements. The emperor replied: "When the enemy comes, join the Commissariat and resist together;

sentences.zh: 敵去，則務農作，勿勞士馬。」

translations.literal: when the enemy leaves, attend to farming — do not weary troops and horses."
translations.idiomatic: when they leave, see to the farming and do not weary the troops and horses."

sentences.zh: 會敵入束城，我軍退渡滹沱而屯。

translations.literal: When the enemy entered Dongcheng, our army withdrew, crossed the Hutuo, and encamped.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy entered Dongcheng, our army fell back across the Hutuo and made camp.

sentences.zh: 思溫勒兵徐行，周軍數日不動。

translations.literal: Siwen led the troops at a measured pace; the Zhou army for several days did not move.
translations.idiomatic: Siwen led his troops forward at a deliberate pace, and the Zhou army held still for days.

sentences.zh: 思溫與諸將議曰：「敵眾而銳，戰不利則有後患。

translations.literal: Siwen discussed with the generals, saying: "The enemy are numerous and sharp; if battle goes ill there will be later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Siwen consulted the generals: "The enemy are numerous and keen — if we fight and fare badly, trouble will follow.

sentences.zh: 不如頓兵以老其師，躡而擊之，可以必勝。」

translations.literal: Better to halt the army and wear down their force, then follow and strike — certain victory can be had."
translations.idiomatic: Better to hold our ground and wear them down, then follow and strike — we can be sure of victory."

sentences.zh: 諸將從之。

translations.literal: The generals followed this plan.
translations.idiomatic: The generals agreed.

sentences.zh: 遂與統軍司兵會，飾他說請濟師。

translations.literal: Thereupon they joined the Commissariat troops, dressed up another plea, and requested relief forces.
translations.idiomatic: They then united with the Commissariat troops and, under another pretext, again asked for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 周人引退，思溫亦還。

translations.literal: The Zhou withdrew; Siwen also returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou withdrew, and Siwen returned as well.

sentences.zh: 已而周主復北侵，與其將傅元卿、李崇進等分道並進，圍瀛州，陷益津、瓦橋、淤口三關，垂迫固安。

translations.literal: Before long the Zhou ruler again invaded north, and with his generals Fu Yuanqing, Li Chongjin, and others advanced by separate routes together, besieged Yingzhou, took the three passes of Yijin, Wanqiao, and Yukou, and pressed close on Gu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Zhou emperor invaded the north again. With Fu Yuanqing, Li Chongjin, and other generals advancing on separate routes, he besieged Yingzhou, captured the passes at Yijin, Wanqiao, and Yukou, and pressed toward Gu'an.

sentences.zh: 思溫不知計所出，但雲車駕旦夕至。

translations.literal: Siwen knew no plan to offer and only said the imperial carriage would arrive any day.
translations.idiomatic: Siwen had no plan to offer and could only say that the emperor's carriage would arrive at any moment.

sentences.zh: 麾下士奮躍請戰，不從。

translations.literal: The troops under his command eagerly leaped forward begging battle; he did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: His men eagerly pressed him to fight; he refused.

sentences.zh: 已而陷易、瀛、莫等州，京畿人皆震駭，往往遁入西山。

translations.literal: Before long Yi, Ying, Mo, and other prefectures fell; people of the capital region were all shaken with terror and often fled into the Western Hills.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, Ying, Mo, and other prefectures soon fell. People throughout the capital region were terrified, and many fled into the Western Hills.

sentences.zh: 思溫以邊防失利，恐朝廷罪己，表請親征。

translations.literal: Siwen, because the border defense had failed, feared the court would blame him and memorialized requesting the emperor lead the campaign in person.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing blame for the border defeat, Siwen memorialized asking the emperor to lead the campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 會周主榮以病歸，思溫退至益津，偽言不知所在。

translations.literal: It happened that the Zhou ruler Rong returned because of illness; Siwen withdrew to Yijin and falsely said he did not know where the enemy were.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou emperor Shizong returned north ill, Siwen withdrew to Yijin and pretended not to know where the enemy were.

sentences.zh: 遇步卒二千餘人來拒，敗之。

translations.literal: He met more than two thousand infantry coming to resist and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He met a body of more than two thousand infantry blocking his way and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 是年，聞周喪，燕民始安，乃班師。

translations.literal: That year, hearing of the Zhou mourning, the people of Yan first grew calm, and he then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when news of the Zhou emperor's death arrived, the people of Yan settled down, and he withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 時穆宗湎酒嗜殺，思溫以密戚預政，無所匡輔，士論不與。

translations.literal: At the time Muzong was sunk in wine and loved killing; Siwen as a close kinsman participated in government yet offered no correction — scholarly opinion did not endorse him.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Muzong drowned himself in wine and delighted in killing, Siwen, though a close kinsman in government, offered no correction — and learned opinion did not approve of him.

sentences.zh: 十九年，春蒐，上射熊而中，思溫與夷離畢牙裏斯等進酒上壽，帝醉還宮。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, at the spring hunt, the emperor shot a bear and hit it; Siwen with Yilibi Yalisi and others offered wine and wished long life; the emperor, drunk, returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In his nineteenth year, at the spring hunt, the emperor shot a bear and hit it. Siwen, Yilibi Yalisi, and others offered wine and wished him long life; the emperor returned to the palace drunk.

sentences.zh: 是夜，為庖人斯奴古等所弒。

translations.literal: That night he was assassinated by the kitchen servant Sinugu and others.
translations.idiomatic: That night he was assassinated by the kitchen servant Sinugu and his accomplices.

sentences.zh: 思溫與南院樞密使高勛、飛龍使女裏等立景宗。

translations.literal: Siwen with Southern Privy Commissioner Gao Xun, Dragon Flight Commissioner Nüli, and others installed Jingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Siwen, together with Southern Privy Commissioner Gao Xun, Dragon Flight Commissioner Nüli, and others, enthroned Emperor Jingzong.

sentences.zh: 保寧初，為北院樞密使，兼北府宰相，仍命世預其選。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoning he was Northern Privy Commissioner, also Northern Chancellery chancellor, and still ordered his line to participate in its selection.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Baoning era he became Northern Privy Commissioner and Northern Chancellery chancellor, and his line was still enrolled in chancellor selection.

sentences.zh: 上冊思溫女為後，加尚書令，封魏王。

translations.literal: The emperor enfeoffed Siwen's daughter as empress, added the post of Minister-in-Chief, and sealed him Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Siwen's daughter empress, appointed him Minister-in-Chief, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 從帝獵閭山，為賊所害。

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor on a hunt at Lü Mountain, he was killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: While accompanying the emperor on a hunt at Lü Mountain, he was killed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 蕭繼先，字楊隱，小字留只哥。

translations.literal: Xiao Jixian, style name Yangyin, childhood name Liuzhige.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Jixian, whose style name was Yangyin and childhood name Liuzhige.

sentences.zh: 幼穎悟，叔思溫命為子，睿智皇后尤愛之。

translations.literal: As a child he was clever; his uncle Siwen adopted him as son; Empress Ruizhi especially loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Clever as a boy, he was adopted as a son by his uncle Siwen, and Empress Ruizhi was especially fond of him.

sentences.zh: 乾亨初，尚齊國公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianheng he married the Princess of Qi and was appointed Chief Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianheng era he married the Princess of Qi and was made Chief Son-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 統和四年，宋人來侵，繼先率邏騎逆境上，多所俘獲，上嘉之，拜北府宰相。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tonghe the Song came to invade; Jixian led border cavalry against the enemy's advance, captured many, the emperor commended him, and he was appointed Northern Chancellery chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tonghe, when the Song invaded, Jixian led border cavalry against their advance, took many captives, and was commended and made Northern Chancellery chancellor.

sentences.zh: 自是出師，繼先必將本府兵先從。

translations.literal: From this time on, whenever armies went out, Jixian always led his bureau's troops in the van.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever the army marched out, Jixian always led his bureau's troops in the van.

sentences.zh: 拔狼山石壘，從破宋軍應州。

translations.literal: He took the stone fort at Langshan and joined in routing the Song army at Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the stone fort at Langshan and helped rout the Song at Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 上南征，取通利軍，戰稱捷力。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned south he took Tongli Army; in battle he was praised for vigorous achievement.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's southern campaign he captured Tongli Army and was praised in battle for his vigor.

sentences.zh: 及親征高麗，以繼先年老，留守上京。

translations.literal: When the emperor personally campaigned against Goryeo, because Jixian was old he was left to guard the Supreme Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned against Goryeo in person, Jixian, now elderly, was left to guard the Supreme Capital.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 繼先雖處富貴，尚儉素，所至以善治稱，故將兵攻戰，未嘗失利，名重戚裏。

translations.literal: Though Jixian dwelt in wealth and honor he still valued frugality and simplicity; wherever posted he was praised for good governance; thus commanding troops in attack and battle he never suffered defeat — his name weighed heavy among imperial kin.
translations.idiomatic: Though wealthy and honored, Jixian still lived plainly. Wherever he was posted he was praised for good governance, and in command he never lost a fight — his reputation stood high among the imperial kin.

sentences.zh: 論曰：嗚呼！

translations.literal: Appreciation says: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Appreciation: Alas!

sentences.zh: 人君之過，莫大於殺無辜。

translations.literal: Among a ruler's faults, none is greater than killing the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Of all a ruler's faults, none is greater than putting the innocent to death.

sentences.zh: 湯之伐桀也，數其罪曰「並告無辜於上下神祇」；

translations.literal: When Tang attacked Jie he counted his crimes, saying "Together reporting the innocent to the spirits above and below";
translations.idiomatic: When Tang attacked Jie, he recited his crimes: "You have together reported the innocent to the spirits above and below";

sentences.zh: 武王之伐紂也，數其罪曰「無辜籲天」；

translations.literal: when Wu attacked Zhou he counted his crimes, saying "The innocent cry to Heaven";
translations.idiomatic: when Wu attacked Zhou, he recited his crimes: "The innocent cry to Heaven";

sentences.zh: 堯之伐苗民也，呂侯追數其罪曰「殺戮無辜」。

translations.literal: when Yao attacked the Miao people, Marquis Lü pursued and counted their crimes, saying "Slaughtering the innocent."
translations.idiomatic: when Yao attacked the Miao, Marquis Lü pursued the charge: "Slaughtering the innocent."

sentences.zh: 跡是言之，夷臘葛之諫，凜凜庶幾古君子之風矣。

translations.literal: Tracing these words, Yilage's remonstrance — stern and imposing — nearly approaches the air of the gentlemen of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by these precedents, Yilige's remonstrance was stern and commanding — nearly the bearing of the gentlemen of old.

sentences.zh: 雖然，善諫者不諫於已然，蓋必先得於心術之微，如察脈者，先其病而治之，則易為功。

translations.literal: Yet those skilled at remonstrance do not remonstrate after the fact has formed; they must first grasp the subtle shifts of the heart-mind — like one who examines the pulse, treating before the illness manifests, then achievement is easy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a skilled remonstrator does not wait until the deed is done; he must catch the subtle turn of mind beforehand — like a physician who treats the pulse before illness breaks out, so the cure is easy.

sentences.zh: 穆宗沈湎失德，蓋其資富強之勢以自肆久矣。

translations.literal: Muzong was sunk in debauchery and lost in virtue — likely he had long relied on the power of wealth and strength to indulge himself.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong sank into debauchery and lost his virtue because he had long leaned on the empire's wealth and strength to indulge himself.

sentences.zh: 使群臣於造次動作之際，引諫彼諍，提而警之，以防其甚，則亦詎至是哉！

translations.literal: Had the ministers at moments of hasty action drawn forth remonstrance and earnest debate, lifted warnings to alert him and guard against extremes — how could it have reached this!
translations.idiomatic: Had his ministers, at every rash impulse, urged remonstrance and debate, lifted warnings before things went too far — how could matters have come to this!

sentences.zh: 於以知護思、思溫處位優重，耽祿取容，真鄙夫矣！

translations.literal: From this one knows that Husi and Siwen, occupying honored stations, clung to salary and sought favor — true petty men!
translations.idiomatic: This shows that Husi and Siwen, for all their high rank, clung to salary and sought favor — nothing but contemptible men!

sentences.zh: 若海璃之折獄，繼先之善治，可謂任職臣歟！

translations.literal: As for Haili's judging of cases and Jixian's good governance — may they be called ministers who fulfilled their duties!
translations.idiomatic: As for Haili's judging of cases and Jixian's good governance — these may be called ministers who did their duty!
